recent_posts.title: Why dropping metric labels to reduce cardinality is a false economy
recent_posts.summary: High cardinality in observability metrics is often treated as a problem to eliminate, but dropping labels means losing the ability to diagnose production issues. Every label represents a dimension of knowledge — merchant IDs, pod IDs, content IDs — and removing them can corrupt data (e.g., breaking Prometheus rate() calculations) or hide which customers are affected during incidents. Modern infrastructure with Kubernetes, autoscaling, and ephemeral pods makes high cardinality inevitable through identity churn. The real issue is whether observability platforms force a trade-off between budget and visibility, taxing teams on cardinality rather than ingestion volume.

recent_posts.title: Introducing the Coralogix CLI: Headless Observability for Every Agent
recent_posts.summary: Coralogix has released the cx CLI, a single binary designed to give AI coding agents direct, structured access to telemetry data from the terminal. Key features include server-side aggregation via DataPrime (handling up to 200M logs), a TOON-based token-optimized output format that reduces token usage by ~90% compared to JSON, semantic field search for schema discovery, multi-team/region fan-out queries, and pre-built skill integrations for 40+ agents including Claude Code, Cursor, and Codex. The tool enables AI agents to perform production investigations across logs, spans, metrics, alerts, and RUM without overloading context windows or requiring knowledge of the underlying data schema.

recent_posts.title: How the Coralogix CLI Adds Production Intelligence to Any Agent for Any Use Case
recent_posts.summary: Coralogix introduces its CLI (`cx`) as a data layer that enables AI coding agents (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, etc.) to query production telemetry efficiently. Three use cases are demonstrated: a FinOps lead analyzing 36 million logs via server-side aggregation to optimize observability costs, a product manager querying Real User Monitoring data to reprioritize a backlog, and a DevOps engineer checking database health before a migration. The CLI uses server-side aggregation via DataPrime, a semantic layer for field discovery, and agent-optimized output (TOON encoding) to minimize token usage. It ships with prebuilt skills for 40+ coding agents and connects to all Coralogix APIs.

recent_posts.title: Real-Time Database Monitoring: Solving Database Latency with Zero-Code eBPF Tracing
recent_posts.summary: eBPF-based instrumentation (OBI by Coralogix) can eliminate the observability blind spot between application and database layers without any code changes or sidecars. By deploying as a Kubernetes DaemonSet, OBI intercepts database traffic at the Linux kernel/syscall boundary and decodes protocols like Couchbase's binary protocol and SQL++ (N1QL) in real time. It enriches telemetry with Kubernetes context, database targets, and operation metadata, then emits OpenTelemetry-compatible metrics and spans. The workflow covers a Database Catalog for RED metrics, trace deep-dives to isolate slow queries, and trace-to-log correlation to reduce MTTR.

recent_posts.title: Observability for Claude Code using OpenTelemetry and Coralogix
recent_posts.summary: Claude Code emits native OpenTelemetry telemetry covering token usage, model costs, tool calls, and code impact signals, but lacks a built-in destination or dashboard. Coralogix integrates directly with Claude Code's OTLP exporter to stream this data into existing observability pipelines in real time. Key signals include token usage broken down by type, code impact metrics (lines added, commits, PRs) correlated with compute spend, and active processing time versus developer review time. This gives engineering and platform teams visibility into who is driving AI costs, which models are being used, and whether spend translates into meaningful output — turning reactive monthly billing surprises into proactive, data-driven decisions.

recent_posts.title: How Kotak811 Revolutionized Digital Banking Observability with Coralogix
recent_posts.summary: Kotak811, the digital banking arm of Kotak Mahindra Bank serving 23 million users, partnered with Coralogix to overhaul its observability stack. Facing data overload from millions of concurrent transactions, the team implemented a 5-phase migration: architectural mapping, observability-as-code via Terraform and Helm in CI/CD pipelines, telemetry unification using OpenTelemetry across 200+ microservices, TCO optimization with Coralogix's Streama technology, and full-stack developer enablement. The architecture routes logs from AWS EKS, EC2, CloudWatch, and CloudTrail through AWS Private Link to Coralogix, with enriched data archived back to S3. Results include a 90-95% reduction in Mean Time to Detection, 30% reduction in observability costs, and automated onboarding ensuring every new microservice is 'born observable'.

recent_posts.title: The Security Trifecta: Operationalizing API Protection with AWS, Wallarm, and Coralogix
recent_posts.summary: APIs have become the primary attack surface for modern enterprises, yet security operations remain fragmented across detection, investigation, and mitigation silos. A 'Security Trifecta' combining AWS (infrastructure), Wallarm (API threat detection), and Coralogix (observability and correlation) is proposed as an integrated solution. Wallarm detects business logic abuse across REST, GraphQL, and gRPC; Coralogix correlates those alerts with infrastructure logs, APM traces, and metrics to reduce alert fatigue and accelerate triage. Real-world breaches at LinkedIn, Okta, and UnitedHealth are cited to illustrate the gaps that each layer addresses.

recent_posts.title: From Vibes to Signals: Observing Your AI Coding Workflow
recent_posts.summary: Agentic coding tools like Claude Code and Codex are now embedded in the critical path of software delivery, yet most teams evaluate their impact purely on gut feel. These tools emit OpenTelemetry telemetry — token usage, tool latency, acceptance rates — that can be routed to an observability backend without any custom instrumentation. By treating the AI coding workflow as an observable system, teams can correlate AI usage with DORA metrics, compare model efficiency by cost-per-commit and acceptance rate, and debug slow or failing agent interactions via distributed traces. A step-by-step guide shows how to connect Claude Code to Coralogix using a cloned integration repo, set environment credentials, and import a pre-built dashboard for org-wide visibility.

recent_posts.title: What “AI-Ready Data” actually means for observability teams
recent_posts.summary: Most observability platforms were designed for human querying, not AI consumption. For AI agents to effectively analyze telemetry data, four architectural capabilities are needed: an expressive query language (like Coralogix's DataPrime), a living schema that tracks field evolution over time, full-fidelity data access without indexing constraints, and governed semantic domains that scope AI investigations. Without these, AI agents hallucinate queries, miss signals in unindexed data, and produce noisy results. Coralogix frames its own architecture — in-stream processing, customer-owned storage in open Parquet format, and dataset-level governance — as purpose-built for this AI-ready data model, with its Olly agent as the practical expression of these capabilities.

recent_posts.title: Code Agents Need Observability
recent_posts.summary: Coralogix has launched Code Agent Observability, a feature that gives engineering teams visibility into how AI coding agents like Claude Code, Codex, and Gemini are being used across their organization. By leveraging native OpenTelemetry support, teams can track token usage, costs, code impact (lines added/removed, PRs opened), tool call decisions, and session activity — all within the existing Coralogix platform. A dedicated dashboard provides cost breakdowns by user, productivity ratios, and the ability to correlate AI usage with production outcomes like incident resolution rates.
